title: inklu
summary: Lightweight open-source libraries for web interfaces: audio, shortcuts, tours, and a dock.

sections.body:
**Four things I wanted to stop rebuilding from scratch.**

Audio feedback, keyboard shortcuts, onboarding tours, and side panels. I needed them in nearly every project, and existing packages were either too heavy or forced a visual theme.

So I extracted them into independent libraries.

sections.heading: The four
sections.body:
- **audio** generates 29 tactile sounds directly in code. Not a single asset file or network request.
- **keys** manages keyboard shortcuts with conflict detection and customizable bindings.
- **tour** handles guided product walkthroughs with full keyboard and screen-reader support.
- **dock** provides URL-synced side panels for dense applications.
sections.caption: Each library has its own docs and a playground.

sections.heading: No design opinions
sections.body: They handle the logic and stay completely out of your styles. If you build clean, minimal interfaces, they drop in with zero resistance.

sections.heading: In production
sections.body:
They power the interfaces for [Rugero](/rugero) and [Jace](/jace). When an edge case shows up in production, it gets fixed at the source.

They currently see around 900 downloads a month on npm.
